ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All directors, shareholders, ultimate beneficial owners (UBOs), and signatories must undergo enhanced due diligence (EDD) before incorporation. The compliance officer must screen against the New Zealand Police Financial Intelligence Unit's sanction and PEP lists, the New Zealand Economic Sanctions Act 2020 register, the United Nations Security Council consolidated sanctions list, the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons (SDN) list, and the EU/UK consolidated financial sanctions lists. PEP status includes foreign, domestic, and international-organisation PEPs, their family members and known close associates. Automated screening hits must be escalated to the AML/CFT compliance officer within 24 hours; false-positive resolutions must be documented. Ongoing transaction monitoring will be established under Part 2 of the AML/CFT Act 2009.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: New Zealand Companies Office - Companies Online (register.companiesoffice.govt.nz)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Names must be in English or Maori; if a non-Latin script is used, a phonetic English transliteration is required. The legal suffix 'Limited' or 'Ltd' is mandatory. The Registrar may reject names that are identical, confusingly similar, or misleadingly similar to an existing name. Four-tier naming conventions require: (1) the proposed name; (2) the legal element; (3) any distinguishing number, letter, or descriptive word; and (4) the omission of any token from the restricted-token list unless ministerial consent is obtained.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Name reservations under Section 26 of the Companies Act 1993 are valid for 20 working days and cannot be extended; a new reservation must be requested if the name is still required. Upon rejection, the applicant has 20 working days to file a written appeal with the Registrar of Companies. The appeal must include the original application reference, a statutory declaration explaining why the name is not misleading or confusingly similar, and any required consent from the relevant regulator. The Registrar must issue a reconsideration decision within 20 working days. If the refusal is upheld, the applicant may appeal to the High Court of New Zealand under section 378 of the Companies Act 1993, or may submit a new name reservation with amended distinguishing words and pay the standard filing fee.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A standard virtual office is permissible only as a registered office address if a physical street address is provided and mail forwarding is operational. However, for a battery safety and UN38.3 testing laboratory, a virtual office is not acceptable as the principal place of business. Inland Revenue and the New Zealand Companies Office require commercial substance, including a leased laboratory, safety certification, and staff presence. A virtual mailbox will likely be rejected by the corporate bank when opening an account and may trigger enhanced AML/CFT review. Therefore, the company must lease dedicated laboratory premises; use of a virtual office creates an estimated 85% probability of bank account refusal or audit penalty.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist: (1) WorkSafe NZ health-and-safety inspection for battery testing hazards; (2) municipal council environmental health visit for hazardous-material storage; (3) Inland Revenue audit of commercial substance and GST registration; (4) Companies Office verification of registered office; (5) Energy Safety confirmatory inspection for UN38.3 test certificates. Quantified risk: moderate-high, estimated 55% chance of an unannounced physical inspection in the first 24 months.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 1993 (New Zealand), especially ss.10-16, s.13(1) (registration of company), s.22 (company name restrictions), and s.120-151 (director duties and consent); Companies (Registered Companies) Regulations 1994; Financial Reporting Act 2013; Health and Safety at Work Act 2015 (relevant to officer responsibilities).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: New Zealand Companies Office, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE), administered through the New Zealand Companies Register (www.companiesregister.govt.nz).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Online Application for Company Incorporation under the Companies Act 1993, including adoption of constitution, consent to act as director, registered office statement, and address for service declaration.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. New Zealand does not require minimum paid-up capital for a standard limited company. The company may be incorporated with nil paid-up capital. No blocked escrow account is required by statute. Any issued share capital and any amount subscribed must be recorded in the share register and handled in accordance with the board resolution.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: AT A MEETING of the Board of Directors of [INSERT COMPANY NAME] LIMITED (the Company) duly convened and held at [registered office address], New Zealand on [date] at [time]. A quorum was present. The Chairperson and the Secretary tabled the Company Constitution, the Certificate of Incorporation, and the share subscription instruments. After due deliberation, the following resolutions were proposed, seconded and unanimously carried: 1. SHARE CAPITAL AND SUBSCRIPTION. RESOLVED that the allotment and issue of [X] ordinary shares at par value [NZD] per share to [SHAREHOLDER NAME] be and is hereby approved. RESOLVED FURTHER that the subscription price shall be payable on call, and that the Directors are authorised to demand, receive and receipt lawful money in satisfaction thereof. RESOLVED FURTHER that the share register and any relevant register of ultimate beneficial owners be duly updated and that share certificates be issued under the Company seal (if present) or counterpart signature in accordance with the Constitution. 2. BANKING AUTHORIZATION. RESOLVED that the Company open such current and deposit accounts with a New Zealand licensed bank as determined by the Managing Director, and that the signing officers with specimen signatures, being [DIRECTOR A], [DIRECTOR B], and [SECRETARY C], be formally registered in the banking mandate. RESOLVED FURTHER that all outgoing payments, including Wire Transfer and Wise instructions, shall be authorised by any two signatories or by one director plus the company secretary, with dual-approval above [NZD 10,000] daily; and that the bank be provided with certified copies of this resolution. 3. REGISTERED OFFICE. RESOLVED that the registered office of the Company be adopted at [ADDRESS] and that the address for service be the same address. RESOLVED FURTHER that the Secretary file all notices with the New Zealand Companies Office and procure the continued availability of the office during ordinary business hours. 4. STATUTORY OFFICER APPOINTMENTS. RESOLVED that [FULL NAME] be appointed Managing Director, [FULL NAME] be appointed Director, and [FULL NAME] be appointed Company Secretary and Compliance Officer, each to hold office subject to the constitution and removal by ordinary/special resolution. RESOLVED FURTHER that the Managing Director be delegated executive powers consistent with the Companies Act 1993, excluding non-reviewable reserved matters of the Board. 5. CONSTITUTION AND STATUTORY COMPLIANCE. RESOLVED that the Constitution be adopted and that the officers, acting jointly and severally, take all steps to register the Company for income tax, GST and employer obligations, obtain New Zealand Business Number records, file incorporations, maintain the statutory registers, appoint auditors if required, and procure public liability and errors and omissions insurance. RESOLVED that the Chairperson certify these resolutions as true and accurate and enter them in the minute book.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pre-Incorporation Name Clearance and Name Reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office via the Companies Register online portal (MBIE)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a name availability search on the New Zealand Companies Register for at least three proposed names. Confirm that the proposed name is not identical or too similar to an existing registered name and does not contravene s.22 of the Companies Act 1993. Names containing terms such as Bank, Trust, University or Government require prior consent or are restricted by law. The applicant must also ensure that no culturally sensitive or contentious phrase is used. Where a restricted word is intended, apply for official consent and retain the approval reference. The name search should be documented with a screen print or certificate reference. This step avoids later rejection and ensures that the company can be registered under the desired commercial identity before the incorporation application is lodged.
required_dossiers: Proposed company name (first, second and third alternatives)
certificate or screen print of Companies Register name availability search
written authority from relevant regulator if restricted word is used
name reservation receipt if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused as identical or undesirable, select an alternative available name or apply to the Registrar for reconsideration with a written explanation. If a restricted word is refused, obtain consent from the relevant regulatory agency and resubmit the name application.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation of Constitution, Share Subscriptions and Director Consents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand legal counsel and corporate governance adviser prior to Companies Office filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the company constitution either in the default form under Schedule 1 of the Companies Act 1993 or as a custom constitutional document covering share classes, director powers, restrictions, board quorum, voting mechanics and indemnity provisions. Obtain executed share subscription agreements from proposed shareholders, specifying number, class and subscription amount. Obtain each proposed director's signed consent to appointment, date of birth, residential address and disclosure of any disqualifying criminal or bankruptcy matters. Ensure that no director is disqualified under ss.151-152 of the Companies Act 1993. The constitution must be dated and adopted by the subscribers or directors before the online application is submitted. All documents should be retained in the company minute book and made available to the Companies Office for inspection if requested.
required_dossiers: Executed constitution (custom or default)
share subscription agreements
shareholder register information
consent to appointment of director and personal identification
disqualification declarations for each director
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Companies Office queries the directors background or constitution, provide a written statutory declaration and any court clearance. Re-execute and correct defective documents and resubmit within the prescribed response window.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Lodgment of Company Incorporation Application and Payment of Filing Fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office, online Companies Register portal with RealMe login
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log in with verified RealMe credentials and complete the online company incorporation application. Enter the approved company name, registered office street address, postal address for service, share structure, director details, shareholder details and constitution election. Attach scanned copies of the executed consent to act as director and the constitution if a custom form is adopted. Verify all personal details against acceptable identification and declare the information truthful. Submit the application and pay the prescribed filing fee by debit or credit card. The Companies Office will issue a Certificate of Incorporation under section 13 and a New Zealand Business Number if the application is complete. The applicant must keep a copy of the approved application receipt and the certificate for subsequent tax and licensing filings.
required_dossiers: RealMe verified identity
approved company name and reservation reference
registered office address and address for service
director and shareholder statutory details
executed constitution (if custom)
fee payment authority
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is returned on a defective data point, correct the field and resubmit within 10 business days. If the application is suspended because of a name objection or third-party caveat, provide the Companies Office with additional legal argument or withdraw and file under a different name.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Registration Tax Registration, NZBN Activation and Statutory Register Maintenance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Inland Revenue New Zealand (IR); New Zealand Companies Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After receiving the Certificate of Incorporation, obtain the New Zealand Business Number (NZBN) from the Companies Register. Register the company with Inland Revenue for income tax using the myIR online service or Form IR596. Register for GST if projected annual turnover exceeds NZD 60,000 and for PAYE employer obligations before hiring any staff. File all shareholder and director information as required by the Companies Office and prepare the annual return calendar. Convene the first board meeting to approve the opening of tax records, appointment of a tax agent, adoption of an accounting software system, and designation of financial year end. Keep a statutory minute book containing the certificate of incorporation, constitution, consents, share register, interests register and the first board resolution. This step ensures the entity has full tax and corporate standing to contract with banks and licensing authorities.
required_dossiers: Certificate of incorporation and NZBN
first board resolution authorizing tax registration
director and shareholder identification
projected turnover and business commencement details
annual return calendar and registered office record
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If IRD registration is delayed, call IR Business and obtain a case reference, then resubmit the online application. If Companies Office annual return first filing is triggered, set a compliance reminder and file before the due date to avoid late fees.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Industrial and Physical Licensing Applications and Bank Account Activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: WorkSafe New Zealand; Fire and Emergency New Zealand; territorial authority building inspectorate; International Accreditation New Zealand; New Zealand licensed banks
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit an application to WorkSafe New Zealand for a Hazardous Substances Location Certificate covering the battery safety testing laboratory, including stored quantities, separation distances, containment areas and certified Safety Data Sheets. Engage an accredited test engineer to review the UN38.3 drop-test equipment, charging stations and thermal abuse chambers. Apply to the territorial authority for any building consent, structural load certification and environmental health approval. Submit an ISO/IEC 17025 accreditation application to International Accreditation New Zealand so that UN38.3 and CE-RED electromagnetic test reports can be commercially recognized. For fire safety, obtain Fire and Emergency New Zealand approval and a building warrant of fitness. Finally, open company bank accounts at a New Zealand licensed bank using the board banking resolution, completing Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009 verification for all controlling persons and arranging wire transfer and Wise payment rail access.
required_dossiers: Hazardous substances inventory and Safety Data Sheets
site plan and fire protection system drawings
building consent and structural certification
IANZ application and laboratory quality manual
Board banking mandate and AML forms
electrical safety certificates under AS NZS 3000
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If WorkSafe or the territorial authority issues a deficiency notice, correct the containment and fire systems within 20 working days and provide photographic evidence and revised engineering certificates. If IANZ identifies non-conformities, implement corrective action and resubmit the quality manual.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: WorkSafe New Zealand; Environmental Protection Authority New Zealand; territorial authority (district/city council); International Accreditation New Zealand (IANZ); Fire and Emergency New Zealand
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Hazardous Substances Location Certificate issued under the Hazardous Substances and New Organisms Act 1996 and WorkSafe Hazardous Substances Locations Notice; ISO/IEC 17025 laboratory accreditation from International Accreditation New Zealand for UN38.3 and CE-RED testing; building and fire safety clearance under the Building Act 2004.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environmental Protection Authority New Zealand; applicable regional council under the Resource Management Act 1991
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Environmental Registration for a small-scale battery testing laboratory where hazardous substance quantities remain below WorkSafe location thresholds and where there is no significant discharge to land, air or water. A full Assessment of Environmental Effects and resource consent are required only if the testing operations exceed quantity thresholds, involve open-air thermal abuse testing, or discharge hazardous waste requiring site-specific conditions. Full Environmental Impact Assessment may become mandatory for large-format lithium cell recycling, warehousing or chemical processing adjacent to sensitive receptors.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharges to trade waste must comply with pH 6.0-9.0, total suspended solids less than or equal to 500 milligrams per litre, biochemical oxygen demand (BOD5) less than or equal to 300 milligrams per litre, and oil and grease less than or equal to 100 milligrams per litre. No wastewater may be discharged to stormwater or ground unless authorised by consent. Airborne volatile organic compound emissions must be captured and controlled if any release exceeds two tonnes per annum. Ambient air quality must meet National Environmental Standard for Air Quality 2004 limits, including PM10 50 micrograms per cubic metre as a 24-hour mean, carbon monoxide 10 milligrams per cubic metre as an 8-hour mean, and nitrogen dioxide 200 micrograms per cubic metre as a 1-hour mean. Hazardous wastes comprising damaged lithium cells, electrolyte, solvent debris and contaminated packaging must be stored in labeled EPA-classified hazardous waste containment and transported to an approved licensed hazardous waste disposal facility. All storage areas must be imperviously bunded and fire-rated in accordance with WorkSafe and Fire and Emergency New Zealand standards.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification and building warrant of fitness under the Building Act 2004 and Fire and Emergency New Zealand Act 2017, including automatic fire alarm, suppression and emergency lighting systems in battery charging and abuse-test areas. Structural load assessment for drop-test and vibration rig platforms with maximum dynamic load calculations. Electrical safety verification under AS/NZS 3000 and AS/NZS 3017 for test bays, including earth continuity, RCD protection and thermal camera inspection for high-energy abuse tests. Health and Safety at Work Act 2015 compliance through worker engagement, emergency response plan, hazardous substances inventory, safe work method statements, PPE requirements and incident notification to WorkSafe for serious harm events.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Inland Revenue Department (Inland Revenue / Te Tari Taake), New Zealand; taxpayer electronic portal: myIR (myIR.ird.govt.nz); entity registration and foreign-company registration: New Zealand Companies Office through the Companies Register and New Zealand Business Number (NZBN); export physical clearance: New Zealand Customs Service (Te Mana Arai o Aotearoa).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a New Zealand-incorporated NZ_LTD, the entity is automatically created with a New Zealand Business Number (NZBN) under the Companies Act 1993 and must separately apply to Inland Revenue for an IRD number; application is made using the prescribed Inland Revenue company IRD number registration process published on ird.govt.nz, and requires company name, Companies Office number, registered office, principal business activity, date of incorporation, director/shareholder details, and New Zealand address for service. For a genuine foreign non-resident entity, the first step is to determine whether it will be 'carrying on business' in New Zealand; if so, it must register as an overseas company with the New Zealand Companies Office under the Companies Act 1993, obtain an NZBN, and then submit the non-resident company IRD number application to Inland Revenue, attaching certified certificate of incorporation, constitution, director and shareholder registers, a New Zealand address for service, and authorisation for a resident tax agent where applicable. The IRD number is the single national Tax Identification Number and is also the GST registration number. If the entity's taxable supplies, including zero-rated supplies, in any 12-month period are expected to exceed NZ$60,000, or if it is a non-resident supplier of remote services to New Zealand-resident consumers above that threshold, a simultaneous GST registration application must be lodged through myIR using the same IRD number. A New Zealand resident agent or address for service should be retained to receive Inland Revenue and Companies Office notices.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: New Zealand does not have a US-style check-the-box election or a general hybrid classification election. A closely held eligible limited company may elect look-through company (LTC) treatment under subpart HB of the Income Tax Act 2007, causing profits and losses to be transparent to shareholders rather than taxed at entity level; otherwise the default is entity-level taxation at the corporate rate. New Zealand has also enacted hybrid and branch mismatch rules in sections FH 1 to FH 17 of the Income Tax Act 2007, and eligible New Zealand corporate groups may elect consolidated group treatment under the Income Tax Act 2007 where they meet the statutory residency and shareholding conditions.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax (GST) under the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: NZ$60,000 of taxable supplies, including zero-rated export supplies, in any 12-month period, or where a reasonable expectation exists that the threshold will be exceeded; the same NZ$60,000 threshold applies to non-resident suppliers of remote services supplied to New Zealand-resident consumers. Registration is compulsory once the threshold is crossed, and voluntary registration is possible from the first dollar when a taxable activity is being carried on.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: There is no real-time fiscal clearance, no mandatory government API telemetry, and no anti-fraud digital stamping regime in New Zealand. GST-registered suppliers must issue a tax invoice containing the statutory particulars set out in the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985, including supplier name, IRD/GST number, invoice date, description of supply, GST-exclusive consideration, GST-inclusive consideration, and the GST component, within 28 days of the supply when a tax invoice is required or requested. Invoicing may be paper-based or electronic, voluntary PEPPOL e-invoicing is available, and GST returns are filed electronically through myIR or Inland Revenue-approved filing gateways.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods exported from New Zealand are zero-rated under section 11(1) of the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985 where the goods are supplied to a person who is not in New Zealand and the supplier exports the goods from New Zealand within 28 days of the time of supply, or the goods are supplied in a customs-controlled area and entered for export. Services, including laboratory and UN38.3 battery safety testing services, are zero-rated under section 11A(1) of the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985 where the services are supplied to a recipient who is not resident in New Zealand and is outside New Zealand at the time of supply, provided the services are not supplied to a fixed establishment of the recipient in New Zealand and do not otherwise fall within a statutory exception such as services connected with land in New Zealand. For the testing laboratory, the key substantiation is the testing contract with the non-resident principal, the final UN38.3 test report or CE-RED electromagnetic test certificate, the commercial invoice marked zero-rated, and evidence that the recipient and payment originate outside New Zealand.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: New Zealand Customs Service export entry lodged electronically through the Customs Trade Single Window, producing a valid export clearance reference for the goods; for goods temporarily imported for testing, the corresponding temporary importation entry and subsequent export entry should be retained
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill naming the New Zealand export supplier, the overseas consignee, the New Zealand port or airport of loading, and the overseas port or airport of discharge
Commercial invoice and sales contract showing the cross-border supply, Incoterms, invoiced currency, and itemised value of the laboratory services or goods
Packing list and, for UN38.3 battery safety cargo, the dangerous goods declaration and relevant transport test certificate

Bank SWIFT credit advice, telegraphic transfer confirmation, or foreign exchange credit confirmation showing receipt of settlement funds from the non-resident buyer; New Zealand GST law does not prescribe a fixed foreign-exchange repatriation deadline, but the 180-day figure is retained here as the pipeline evidence benchmark

For services: signed testing agreement with the non-resident client, final test report, tax invoice annotated 'zero-rated export', and a tax residence certificate or statutory declaration from the recipient confirming non-residence outside New Zealand at the time of supply
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: New Zealand law does not impose a separate statutory 180-day foreign-currency repatriation deadline for GST zero-rating; the numerical field represents the dossier's documentary-evidence benchmark. If a supply is not actually zero-rated or the required export evidence is not held, Inland Revenue can assess GST at 15% on the full consideration through a default assessment under the Tax Administration Act 1994, disallow associated input tax claims, and recover the resulting interest and penalties. Use of money interest (UOMI) runs from the original return due date; shortfall penalties may apply at 20% for lack of reasonable care, 20% for an unacceptable tax position, 40% for gross carelessness, 100% for an abusive tax position, and 150% for evasion. False statements made to the New Zealand Customs Service can also attract penalties under the Customs and Excise Act 2018 and prosecution. Inland Revenue may amend assessments within the four-year statutory amendment window for non-fraudulent matters, with no time limit for fraud or evasion, and may retrospectively claw back GST refunds previously issued on unsubstantiated zero-rated supplies.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: New Zealand operates under a freely floating exchange rate regime with no statutory foreign exchange controls, no exchange surrender requirements, and no prior approval for inward or outward capital movements. The Reserve Bank of New Zealand acts as the central bank and prudential regulator but does not impose convertibility restrictions on current account transactions such as trade-related payments, testing service fees, royalties, or capital account flows such as equity injections, dividend remittances, and shareholder loan repayments. Profit repatriation by a non-resident shareholder is generally permissible without exchange control approval; the practical hurdles are corporate tax compliance, financial reporting consistency, and standard AML/CFT verification of the receiving bank. An NZ Ltd trading as a battery safety testing laboratory may hold foreign currency accounts with New Zealand trading banks, invoice clients in USD, EUR, or CNY, and convert proceeds through the domestic interbank market at market-determined rates. No conversion ratio or mandatory channel exists. The absence of capital controls is supported by the OECD code of liberalisation and New Zealand's commitment to free cross-border investment. However, the bank still must perform customer due diligence and suspicious transaction reporting under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009. Therefore, while convertibility is not legally restricted, the operational documentary base must prove the underlying commercial, financial, and beneficial ownership structure to satisfy the financial institution's compliance committee.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Not applicable. New Zealand imposes no statutory export proceeds surrender rule, no forced conversion timeline, and no mandatory conversion ratio. Exporters may retain foreign currency receipts offshore or in onshore foreign currency accounts without restriction. For New Zealand tax purposes, income must be converted into New Zealand dollars using an acceptable exchange rate when recognising revenue.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account and NZD Business Transaction Account
Corporate Currency Account (NZD and foreign currency)
Business Clearing Account and Offshore Currency Account
Business Transaction Account and Foreign Currency Account
NZD Business Account with limited foreign currency capability

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Wise, the New Zealand-founded fintech, is regulated as a financial service provider under the Financial Service Providers Act 2008 but is not a registered bank under the Reserve Bank of New Zealand Act 1989. It cannot provide deposit-taking banking services, capital verification, trade finance, or regulatory-era physical branch services. As a payment and clearing rail, Wise is legally viable in New Zealand because there is no FX-control prohibition on using non-bank electronic money institutions, and it can be effective for low-value cross-border testing fee collections or supplier payments. However, it is not an acceptable substitute for a tier-1 domestic commercial bank as the primary treasury custodian for a UN38.3 battery safety testing laboratory. The entity should maintain its core operating account with a New Zealand trading bank and use EMIs only as a secondary liquidity clearing rail, with strict governance to ensure inbound capital contributions are never settled through unregulated or non-bank channels.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Under the New Zealand AML/CFT regime, there is no absolute statutory mandate that every director must physically appear in a bank branch. The prescribed customer due diligence can be completed through a combination of electronic identity verification, video conferencing, and notarially certified copies of passports, board resolutions, and proof of address. For a structurally standard NZ Ltd with local directorship, remote onboarding is generally feasible with a bank-approved verification platform. Some tier-1 banks may still require an in-branch interview for non-resident directors, high-risk ownership chains, or accounts involving significant cross-border capital movements. Remote consular proxy opening is accepted in practice by several New Zealand banks as long as the director's identity documents are certified by a notary, consul, or qualified legal professional and the electronic KYC audio-video session is completed.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opacity of beneficial ownership behind a non-resident shareholding chain in a laboratory entity with a New Zealand bank account
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified certificate of incorporation and current company extract, notarised register of members, beneficial ownership declaration, trust deed and trustee service provider warranty if any trust holds shares, 12 months of bank statements for the ultimate beneficial owners, independent source of wealth letter from a licensed accountant, CV and professional reference for each director, and an organisational chart showing the natural persons behind the NZ Ltd.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade surveillance filter flags battery testing terminology such as UN38.3, drop test, lithium metal, or energy storage as potentially dual-use or hazardous goods.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: ISO/IEC 17025 laboratory accreditation certificate, scoped test schedule, UN38.3 test summary report from a recognised laboratory, material safety data sheet for the battery cells, product specification sheets demonstrating civil sector use, a client end-use declaration, and a written statement that no defence, military, aerospace, or nuclear application is served. If any controlled testing equipment is imported, include New Zealand Customs and MPI import permits and the relevant export authorisation from the shipper country.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Suspected mismatch between a low initial share capital and high-value test equipment purchases creating a shadow loan or undisclosed financing concern.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Share subscription agreement, bank SWIFT MT103 confirmation showing inbound equity, updated NZ Companies Office share register, board resolution approving the capital expenditure, audited or reviewed financial statements projected for 12 months, vendor quotations and proforma invoices for test chambers and calibration instruments, lease agreements and capital lease schedules, and a statutory declaration confirming no undisclosed lender has security or control rights.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk outbound payments to overseas calibration laboratories, OEM equipment suppliers, or subcontractors in jurisdictions on the bank's enhanced due diligence list.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Know Your Supplier file for each counterparty containing registration certificate, regulatory licence, bank details in the supplier's own name, third-party sanctions and adverse media screening report, underlying testing service agreement or purchase order, commercial invoice, bill of lading or airway bill, inspection certificate, and a clear statement of the business rationale for each cross-border disbursement to allow the bank to complete enhanced due diligence and monitor transactions.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital contributions should be routed as SWIFT MT103 wire transfers into a dedicated capital escrow account held with a tier-1 New Zealand bank. The remittance instruction must carry a transparent purpose code and description such as Equity Contribution for NZ Ltd and include the unique shareholder reference. In New Zealand there is no exchange control approval, but the bank will require the corporate resolution, subscription agreement, and updated share register before the funds are released from escrow. After the funds clear, a New Zealand chartered accountant should issue a capital verification certificate confirming the share issue proceeds are received. This certificate becomes the core treasury evidence for subsequent repatriation of dividends or shareholder loan repayments because it establishes the clean source of funds. For non-equity service revenue, the incoming wire should be referenced as Testing Service Fee and matched to the relevant commercial invoice and contract to prevent the bank classifying the receipt as a capital transaction.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For cross-border testing service payments and laboratory equipment purchases, the primary clearing rails are SWIFT MT103 for direct bank-to-bank transfers, commercial letters of credit for high-value imported calibration equipment or custom-built battery test chambers, and documentary collections for lower-risk repeat supplies. The NZ Ltd should maintain a New Zealand dollar operating account for domestic fees and separate foreign currency accounts to settle supplier invoices in USD, EUR, or CNY without unnecessary conversion. All outbound disbursements must be supported by a purchase order, commercial invoice, shipping or service delivery evidence, and bank KYC documentation for the beneficiary. If using an LC, the bank will verify the underlying trade documents and apply UCP600 rules. For payments to countries where the bank does not correspond directly, the bank will route through a correspondent bank, and the entity must include the correct BIC and account details to avoid regulatory holds.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable foreign exchange forward contracts up to 12 months for USD, EUR, CNY, GBP, and AUD against NZD, subject to the bank's existing credit and margin requirements because the laboratory has a genuine commercial exposure from multi-currency testing revenue and procurement costs.
Foreign exchange swaps for short-term liquidity management, including spot/forward and forward/forward structures to cover inflow-outflow gaps.
Plain vanilla currency options such as NZD/USD collars for protecting budgeted margins on fixed-price international testing contracts while retaining upside through the option premium.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) limited to illiquid or restricted emerging market currencies where an onshore deliverable forward cannot be legally settled; NDFs must be supported by a documented underlying exposure to a specific trade payable or receivable.

Cross-currency swaps only for long-term capital asset financing if the bank offers a matched deal and the entity can evidence a committed FX stream; however, for a testing laboratory of this scale these are not expected to be necessary.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Companies, New Zealand Companies Office (MBIE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due by the last day of the company's registration month (the month of the incorporation anniversary); filing opens 30 days prior and the Companies Office issues a reminder notice 1 month in advance.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of NZD 50 (USD 32) after 28 days; failure to file within 12 months triggers a Notice of Intention to Remove; unless good cause is shown within 20 working days, the company is struck off and dissolved, with assets vesting in the Crown and directors retaining liability for fines up to NZD 10,000.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Audited Financial Statements (filing required only for non-small, overseas-owned, or large companies)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Companies, New Zealand Companies Office (MBIE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after the company's balance date (typically 31 March for domestic entities); for overseas-owned companies, further reporting to Inland Revenue under the Financial Reporting Act 2013 may apply.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Offence under section 215 Companies Act 1993; daily fine up to NZD 500 per director for continuing failure, court-imposed penalties up to NZD 10,000 plus NZD 2,000 per day, and administrative removal from the register after persistent default.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Director and Shareholder Register Amendment Lodgements (event-driven within annual maintenance)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Any transfer or allotment of shares, appointment/cessation of a director, or change of registered office must be lodged within 10 working days of the change; the annual return provides the annual confirmation of the register.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-lodgement subjects the company and every director to default fines of NZD 50 per document with continuing penalties; knowingly inaccurate register filings may lead to prosecution with fines up to NZD 50,000 under the Companies Act 1993.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Independent certified CPA audit is mandatory for any New Zealand limited company that does not qualify as a small company under Section 2 of the Financial Reporting Act 2013. A small company is one that, in each of the two preceding accounting periods, does not exceed at least two of: (i) NZD 3 million book value of total assets; (ii) NZD 6 million of total revenue; (iii) 30 full-time employees. Audit is also compulsory for all 'large' companies (e.g., issuers, companies with NZD 40 million assets / NZD 60 million turnover / 250+ employees, or with 25% or more overseas shareholding) and in any case where shareholders pass a resolution requiring an audit. For this battery safety-LAB entity, a mandatory audit is triggered when any two of the NZD 3M/NZD 6M/30-headcount thresholds are met for two consecutive years.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: New Zealand Generally Accepted Accounting Practice (NZ GAAP) mandated by the External Reporting Board (XRB). Tiers applicable: Tier 1 - Full NZ IFRS for publicly accountable entities; Tier 2 - NZ IFRS with Reduced Disclosure Regime (RDR) for entities with no public accountability but not SME; Tier 3 - NZ SME IFRS (for small-to-medium companies); Tier 4 - simplified cash-basis reporting for qualifying entities. The testing laboratory will generally apply Tier 2 or Tier 3 (NZ IFRS RDR/SME) unless it qualifies as a large entity requiring Tier 1.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: New Zealand does not operate a separate UBO register for ordinary private companies; the Annual Return to the Companies Office constitutes the annual confirmation of the registered members. Any shareholding transfer or allotment must be recorded in the company's own Register of Members and lodged with the Registrar within 10 working days of the event, which provides a 30-day reconciliation window with the annual return cycle. If the company acts as a reporting entity under the AML/CFT Act 2009, an annual UBO identification and verification update must be kept on board files and made available to compliant authorities upon request.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 270 to USD 600 per year (NZD 400 to NZD 1,000) for a registered office and corporate agent in New Zealand, including annual return preparation support.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 5,500 to USD 16,500 per year (NZD 8,000 to NZD 24,000) for a statutory audit of a mid-size NZ company; nil audit fee applies if the company qualifies for the small-company exemption and no shareholder-required audit is adopted.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: New Zealand applies a flat 28% corporate tax rate with no general patent box; however, qualifying R&D expenditure is eligible for a 15% refundable R&D tax credit under the R&D Tax Incentive regime. Certain commercial activities may also qualify for the 20% Minimum Tax Rule adjustment, but no free-zone dividends apply. Non-resident companies deriving New Zealand sourced income are assessable only on that New Zealand sourced income; no deemed repatriation is applied absent actual remittance.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form IR4 (Company Income Tax Return) filed electronically via Inland Revenue's MyIR and e-File portal (ir-files).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The IR4 must be filed by the 7th day of the 7th month after the company's balance date. For a standard 31 March balance date, the statutory deadline is 7 July in the same income year. Tax agents may obtain extension deadlines under IRD concession but the statutory due date controls automatic late filing penalties.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Income from trading, sales, services, testing fees, and any gross business revenue derived by the NZ Ltd in the course of its dangerous goods UN38.3 drop testing and CE-RED electromagnetic laboratory operations.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident-owned NZ Ltd must report all New Zealand sourced gross income, including fees charged to overseas clients for physical testing services physically performed in New Zealand. If the testing is performed offshore or the services are provided from a foreign PE, the income may be allocated outside New Zealand; otherwise the full New Zealand source amount is taxable. Adjustments must be made for deductible expenses directly incurred in producing assessable income; however, amounts paid to non-resident associates for marketing or procurement commissions require transfer pricing substantiation to avoid disallowance.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Interest income, dividend income, royalties, and other non-trading income derived by the company.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Gross interest and royalties derived from New Zealand sources must be included. If the recipient is a non-resident shareholder, NRWT obligations may arise at the payment stage; but the company must still account for assessable income on an accrual basis unless a specific statutory exclusion applies. For intercompany interest income from a non-resident parent, the rate and amount must satisfy the OECD aligned New Zealand transfer pricing rules under ITA 2007 sections GC 13-GC 15.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total expenses, excluding tax depreciation and interest adjusted for apportionment, including laboratory rent, salaries to approved testing engineers, UN38.3 certification equipment depreciation, CE-RED testing consumables, power, and laboratory accreditation fees.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deductions are allowed only to the extent the expenses are incurred in deriving assessable income and are not of a capital nature. Cross-border management fees or head-office cost recharges paid to the non-resident parent are deductible only if the services were actually rendered, the fee is at arm's length under the New Zealand transfer pricing rules, and the Recharge is documented contemporaneously. A non-resident company's branch in New Zealand would only deduct expenses attributable to the New Zealand PE. The NZ Ltd must apply section DA 1 and associated apportionment rules; disallowed entertainment and non-business expenditure should be adjusted.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net accounting profit (or loss) before tax adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The starting point is NZ GAAP (IRS NZ IAS 1 equivalent) financial statements, but any items excluded by tax law must be reconciled. For non-resident shareholders, any accounting profit not repatriated stays in the company and is not automatically taxable to the shareholder; but the company's net profit will feed distributable reserves and eventual dividend NRWT.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Adjustments to accounting profit: non-deductible expenses, exempt income, tax depreciation, loss carry-forward utilisation, R&D tax credit clawbacks, and any transfer pricing adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Add back non-deductible fines, bribes, overseas education expenses, and excessive director fees. Subtract exempt dividends and non-assessable gains. Apply the correct tax depreciation rate for laboratory equipment (e.g., UN38.3 drop test rigs and radio-frequency chambers). A non-resident-owned company claiming R&D credits must confine eligible activities to those satisfying the New Zealand R&D Tax Incentive, including core R&D activities on battery safety parameters; administrative testing that does not involve uncertain research activities must be excluded.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income calculation: total assessable income less total allowable deductions and available loss carry-forwards.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Ensure loss continuity rules are satisfied under ITA 2007 sections IA 5-IA 7. A change in ultimate non-resident ownership of more than 51% can extinguish loss carry-forwards unless the business continues with substantially the same assets and activities. If the NZ Ltd has issued non-resident shares, the 49% continuity threshold may be hard to maintain when offshore investors subscribe; careful tracking of share register movements is mandatory. The resulting taxable income is then multiplied by 28%.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits: PAYE on wages, RWT on interest income, Dividend Withholding Credits, R&D tax credits, and foreign income tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident-owned NZ Ltd may claim Resident Withholding Tax (RWT) credits on its own NZ interest income. Foreign income tax credits are available for overseas taxes paid on income that is also assessable in New Zealand, but the credit is limited to the New Zealand tax attributable to that foreign income. R&D credits are offset against tax before residual payment. Ensure no credit is claimed for NRWT withheld from shareholder loans, as that is a shareholder-level prepayment rather than company income tax credit.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Residual income tax payable (or refundable), being taxable income at 28% less tax credits and R&D incentives.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If a credit arises, Inland Revenue will refund only after the return is assessed; non-resident-owned companies should not import any refund planning as a mechanism to defer tax. Provisional tax instalments must also be reconciled; a non-resident company with high testing revenue must pay provisional tax in three instalments if residual income tax exceeds NZD 2,500.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Imputation credit account (ICA) closing balance and dividend information.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The NZ Ltd (if a New Zealand resident company) must maintain an imputation credit account. Any dividend paid to a non-resident shareholder will require Non-Resident Withholding Tax (NRWT) at the applicable rate unless a treaty reduction applies. The company must complete ICA returns (IR4J) and must not attach imputation credits to dividends paid to non-residents beyond the permitted ratio; doing so triggers a further tax liability under the imputation rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: International disclosure schedule: any interest in a foreign company, foreign investment, or cross-border related-party dealings.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the NZ Ltd has input from a non-resident parent or sister companies, it must disclose related-party transactions on the IR4's international sections. Under the OECD Country-by-Country reporting threshold, if the worldwide group has annual consolidated revenue of EUR 750 million or more, the NZ constituent entity may be required to file CbC Report notification. Failure to disclose intercompany arrangements may expose the company to audit and penalty.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-resident dividend withholding payment (if any) and any dividends paid by the entity during the year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The IR4 asks the company to indicate whether dividends were paid to non-residents during the year. The gross amount of those dividends, NRWT deducted (at 30% standard or treaty reduced rate), and the date of payment are recorded. Undistributed profits are not subject to NRWT, but the company must not convert loans or unpaid management fees into disguised dividends to avoid NRWT; the anti-avoidance power may recharacterise debt as equity.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Signature and executor declaration by the director or branch manager.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Every IR4 must be certified by a person who knows the company's affairs. A non-resident director who signs a false return triggers personal liability; New Zealand law treats the knowing signature as a representation that the return is true and correct. Directors should review the full return and related schedules before authorising electronic lodgement through MyIR.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalties: an initial automatic penalty of NZD 250 for each late instalment or return, plus an additional 1% per month of unpaid residual tax up to a maximum of 10% (for companies) or 15% if the taxpayer has a history of non-compliance. Underpayment penalties include Interest on Underpaid Tax (imputed interest) at the statutory prescribed interest rate (currently around 10.14% per annum). A knowingly incorrect return triggers an evasion penalty of up to 150% of the resulting shortfall, and, under sections 143A and 143B of the Tax Administration Act 1994, deliberate evasion can result in criminal liability with fines of up to NZD 50,000 and imprisonment. Directors can be held jointly and severally liable for unpaid PAYE and GST under the PAYE responsibilities and under the Companies Act 1993 for reckless trading.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 30% (Non-Resident Withholding Tax on dividend payments to non-residents, unless reduced under an applicable Double Tax Agreement).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim reduced dividend, interest, or royalty withholding tax under an applicable New Zealand DTA, the non-resident beneficial owner must provide to the NZ payer: (i) a valid Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the competent authority of their residence jurisdiction; (ii) a completed IRD Form IR451 (Notice of Non-Resident Withholding Tax Reduction) for that particular payment or an approved declaration; and (iii) a written statement of beneficial ownership confirming that the recipient is the economic owner and not an agent, nominee, or conduit. The payer must retain these documents for at least seven years. Inland Revenue must be satisfied that the recipient has no New Zealand PE to which the income is attributable, or, if a PE exists, the treaty may not apply to those profits. For dividends from a New Zealand company, treaty rates generally range from 15% to 5% depending on the percentage of shareholding and the specific treaty; for example, under the US-NZ treaty, a 15% rate applies to portfolio dividends and 5% to a 10%+ corporate shareholder, but application requires proper certification before the payment date to avoid over-withholding.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Interest paid to non-residents attracts NRWT at 15% under New Zealand domestic law, but most DTA rates are 10% or 0% for government entities; approved issuance rules exclude certain publicly offered bonds. Royalties paid to non-residents attract NRWT at 15% under domestic law, with DTA reductions typically to 10% (e.g., US, UK, Australia treaty rates vary). To access treaty relief on royalties, the payer must prove the recipient is resident in the treaty country and that the royalty is derived in connection with a New Zealand source. No DTA relief is available for royalties paid to a resident of a non-treaty jurisdiction. The company must physically withhold and remit NRWT to Inland Revenue at the time of the payment, even if a treaty reduction is anticipated; a refund can be sought if over-withheld. Interest payments to associated non-resident lenders must also meet transfer pricing arm's length rates, otherwise the excessive interest is recharacterised as a disguised dividend subject to dividend NRWT.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: NZD 1,000,000 aggregate cross-border related-party transactions in a single income year triggers the expectation of contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation under the New Zealand Inland Revenue's administrative guidelines, with higher-risk or large multinational groups required to prepare OECD-standard Local File and Master File documentation.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: New Zealand has no standalone Economic Substance Regulation similar to UAE or BVI, but it applies the OECD 'economic substance' and 'beneficial ownership' concepts through anti-avoidance rules (ITA 2007 section BG 1 and section GA 1), the general anti-avoidance rule (GAAR), transfer pricing rules, and the 'core income-generating activities' (CIGA) analysis under the relevant DTA. A shell company without premises, personnel, testing facilities, or business risk will fail the economic substance test for claiming treaty benefits or intercompany service fees. For a UN38.3 battery safety laboratory, true economic substance requires a physical lab in New Zealand with qualified testing engineers, actual test logs, controlled equipment calibration, safety incident protocols, and active certification activities. The New Zealand Inland Revenue will disregard artificial structures and attribute income to the jurisdiction where the real activities are performed.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion by Misdeclaring Offshore Fees
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The NZ Ltd establishes a Hong Kong or Singapore cost-plus service entity that invoices the NZ testing lab at an inflated price for 'marketing, consulting, or battery technology know-how' with no actual personnel or activity in those jurisdictions. The NZ entity claims the excessive fees as deductions, shifting New Zealand taxable profit offshore while the same services are supplied by New Zealand staff. The non-resident parent also uses circular invoicing to prevent the NZ company from generating accounting profit while still distributing dividends out of accumulated tax-paid earnings.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Inland Revenue will apply sections GB 1, GC 13-GC 15 and section GC 21 (transfer pricing adjustments) of the Income Tax Act 2007, plus the general anti-avoidance rule under section BG 1. The shortfall penalty is up to 150% of the tax avoided for evasion; a 20% penalty for unacceptable tax avoidance; and a 40% penalty for gross carelessness. For evading NZD 40,000 or more, criminal prosecution can be brought under sections 143A/143B of the Tax Administration Act 1994.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Under the Companies Act 1993, directors may be personally liable for loss caused to the company by reckless trading (s.135) and for allowing the company to incur obligations that the director knows it cannot fulfil (s.136). In tax evasion cases, the courts may pierce the corporate veil if the company is a mere facade or sham. Directors who knowingly authored or signed false transfer pricing documents face criminal imprisonment of up to 5 years, fines up to NZD 50,000, and disqualification from being director. Directors may also receive an asset freezing order or were subject to a New Zealand Inland Revenue blacklisting under the Government's serious crime asset recovery provisions. Civil restitution is available for taxes, penalties, and legal fees, and directors who attempted to strip company assets to avoid tax can have their personal bank accounts garnished.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company with No Economic Substance in New Zealand
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The entity registers as a New Zealand company but maintains no physical lab, no lease, no full-time technical staff, and no testing equipment. It issues UN38.3 test certificates and CE-RED compliance reports bearing a New Zealand address while all actual testing is performed in mainland China or Taiwan. The company also declares itself tax resident in New Zealand solely to obtain treaty benefits on outbound payments to non-resident shareholders, but no Core Income-Generating Activities occur in New Zealand.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Inland Revenue may reassess the entity as a non-resident company or treat it as a sham under common law and section BG 1. It will deny treaty relief under the relevant DTA by reason of no PE or no beneficial ownership. Fines for false certification and operating without the required statutory testing laboratory accreditation (IECEE / ISO 17025) include revocation of accreditation and prosecution under the Fair Trading Act and the Electricity Safety Regulations. The tax shortfall penalty is 150%, and the company may be struck off under the Companies Act 1993 for operating a sham.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can be personally liable under section 300 Companies Act 1993 for false statements or fraudulent conduct; also under the Financial Reporting Act and Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act if the fake lab receives funds. The veil is pierced when the director uses the company as an instrument for fraud; the director may be jailed for up to 14 years for forgery of safety-test certificates under the Crimes Act 1961. New Zealand courts may issue a travel ban and 'Director Blacklisting' under the Companies Office regime, preventing re-entry into the jurisdiction. Personal assets are subject to a civil asset freeze and restitution order for all profits derived from the fraudulent certificates.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML and Corruption Violation: Accepting Proceeds from Non-Resident Shell Client for Fraudulent UN38.8 'Pass' Certification
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The laboratory knowingly accepts fares from a client owned by a politically exposed person (PEP) from a high-risk jurisdiction. The client pays a premium via Wise or wire transfer to obtain a fraudulent UN38.3 test report stating that unsafe and unverified lithium-ion batteries passed the drop, thermal, and electrical tests. The NZ Ltd also fails to file Suspicious Transaction Reports under the AML/CFT obligations and does not perform customer due diligence on the beneficial owners of the client entity. The payment is routed to a personal bank account of the director or to an overseas trustee.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009, a reporting entity faces fines up to NZD 10 million for serious breaches and directors face fines up to NZD 250,000 and up to 7 years' imprisonment for wilful blindness. The Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE) may cancel the testing laboratory license and ISO 17025 accreditation. The fraudulent certification is also a crime under the Crimes Act 1961, with imprisonment up to 7 years for obtaining registration by deception. If the product enters the EU and causes harm, criminal liability under the CE-RED regulation and the New Zealand Product Safety Standards could add NZD 500,000 penalties per offence.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knew of money laundering through the compromised test certificates are personally liable under section 39 of the AML/CFT Act. The corporate veil is pierced under the sham/fraud exception; the director is personally liable for disgorgement of all testing fees and the cost of any consumer injury claims. A travel ban (Blacklisting) can be imposed under the Proceeds of Crime Act 1991 and a director convicted of a money laundering offence can receive imprisonment for 14 years. The director is barred from managing a company for up to 10 years, personal goods are subject to a proceeds-of-crime confiscation order, and the director is jointly and severally liable for the company's unpaid tax and penalties through the Tax Administration Act s.162.
